findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch name out of the shell
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax, such as `main; id`, `exec()` executes the suffix with the application's privileges. Even legal branch-name metacharacters such as `&` can alter execution and detach `git` from the returned child lifecycle. Retain argument-separated `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` or otherwise avoid invoking a shell.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the Git child’s lifecycle instead of returning a shell
findings.body:
`exec` returns the shell process, not reliably the `git` process. For a legal Git branch containing `&` (for example `slow&true`), POSIX shells can background `git show slow` and exit after `true`; callers then observe `exit` before Git finishes, and `.kill()` cannot cancel the orphaned Git process. `execFile` directly tracked and cancelled Git.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep branch names out of the shell
findings.body:
`exec` interpolates `branch` into a shell command. Any caller-controlled value such as `main; touch /tmp/pwned` executes arbitrary commands with the application’s privileges instead of being passed solely to Git.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch name out of a shell command
findings.body:
`exec()` runs the interpolated string through a shell. If an untrusted branch value reaches this exported function on Unix—for example, `nonexistent;id`—the appended command executes with the application’s privileges. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` passed the value as one argument and did not interpret shell metacharacters.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
